bib.title: Chapter 8. Addressing Constraints (Generative AI Design Patterns)
bib.venue: book chapter (O'Reilly, Generative AI Design Patterns)

question: How can an LLM application be made to fit cost, latency, hardware, throughput and memory constraints in production?
contributions: Pattern 24 Small Language Model: distillation, quantization, speculative decoding
Pattern 25 Prompt Caching: client-side response and semantic caches, server-side prefix and context caches
Pattern 26 Inference Optimization: continuous batching, speculative decoding, prompt compression
Pattern 27 Degradation Testing: TTFT, EERL, TPS, RPS plus scalability, stress and load testing
Pattern 28 Long-Term Memory: working, episodic, procedural and semantic memory, with Mem0

limits: Single-run, single-example demonstrations; no variance, seeds, or quality metrics for distillation or quantization (quality described as 'significantly improved' and 'looks identical').
Hardware, model and server for the continuous batching (23.07x) and speculative decoding (14.2%) runs are in the repo, not the chapter.
Vendor figures for caching and batching (90%, 85%, 80%, 50%, 37%, 28%) are cited without references.
Authors concede speculative decoding can be slower than the large model alone if num_speculative_tokens is too large.
Authors concede distilled students lose generality, inherit teacher biases, and quantization hardware kernel support varies.
Semantic caching trades nuance for hits and needs a similarity threshold; multitenant caches can leak across users.
Dated: vLLM speculative_model argument, model names (Gemma 3, Llama 4 Scout, Claude 3.7 Sonnet), June 2025 GPU pricing.
Chapter has internal slips: Pattern 26 calls SLM 'Pattern 25'; Summary calls Pattern 27 'Inference Distribution Testing'; Table 8-2 says 'speculative coding'.
practices: Prototype with a frontier model, log the prompts, then distil a small model on those prompts (Pattern 24, Option 1).
Check whether a 4-bit version of a self-hosted model loses much accuracy before paying for full precision (Option 2).
Use speculative decoding for lower latency without retraining; tune num_speculative_tokens (Patterns 24 and 26).
Cache client-side to cut total latency; use server-side prefix caching to cut TTFT, and put stable text first in the prompt (Pattern 25, 27).
Include a user identifier in the cache key or system prompt in multitenant systems, and invalidate the cache when the model version changes (Pattern 25, Considerations).
Submit all requests to the inference server so continuous batching can fill GPU slots, rather than looping one at a time (Pattern 26).
Use hard prompt compression with a reconstruction check and evaluation suite; soft compression is model specific (Pattern 26).
Measure TTFT, EERL (P50/P95/P99), TPS and RPS, find the degradation point not just failure, and run scalability, stress and load tests (Pattern 27).
To cut TTFT: shorten the prompt, cache the prefix, reduce max context window, put dynamic text (RAG results) late (Pattern 27).
Trim working memory by token limit keeping valid message pairs and the system prompt; write memories in a background thread; deploy Mem0 as a microservice (Pattern 28).

terms.definition: fine-tune a smaller model on the larger model's responses to problem-specific inputs
a smaller draft model proposes tokens and the larger target model verifies them in parallel, falling back to its own token when it disagrees
the provider stores common parts of a prompt and reuses previously computed internal model states for those parts
a cache searched for queries that are similar, not only exactly the same
requests are pulled from a queue and slotted into the GPU as soon as GPU cores free up, at the granularity of individual forward passes
the time between the submission of the request to the LLM and the generation of the first token of the response
end-to-end request latency: the time to generate the complete response, including queueing time, network latencies and creation time of the KV cache
the total output tokens per second throughput of the system
the average number of requests that can be successfully completed by the system in one second
capacity to store and retrieve messages from the current session
store all messages in a persistent store and search for ones relevant to the current query, primarily based on recency
capacity to store and retrieve system instructions and user-profile attributes used to create instructions
capacity to store and retrieve information primarily based on content

distillation_loss = torch.nn.functional.kl_div(
    torch.log_softmax(student_logits, dim=-1),
    torch.softmax(teacher_logits, dim=-1),
    reduction='batchmean'
) * (self.temperature ** 2)
loss = (1 - self.alpha) * task_loss + self.alpha * distillation

quantization_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
    load_in_4bit=True,
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.float16,
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
    bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
)

llm = LLM(
    model="google/gemma-2-9b-it",
    tensor_parallel_size=1,
    speculative_model="google/gemma-2-2b-it",
    num_speculative_tokens=5,
)

def _get_cache_key(self, prompt: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.md5(prompt.encode()).hexdigest()

trim_messages(

    strategy="last",
    token_counter=ChatOpenAI(MODEL_ID),
    max_tokens=1000,
    start_on="human",
